title: Serpentine quant bottleneck hunt — kernel heuristics and cache interactions
content:
Status
------
Working notes from an exploratory sweep investigating intermittent throughput and tail-latency regressions seen after enabling AWQ/GPTQ kernels in the nightly runner. The behaviour looks sensitive to input ordering and KV cache residency; this doc captures the experimental design we used (the "serpentine sweep"), results summary, hypotheses, and short-term mitigations.

Motivation
----------
We rolled out a kernel-backed quantization selector that can pick AWQ/GPTQ/INT8/FP8 kernels per-model. Nightly smoke runs show ~1–6% lower average throughput and occasional p95 spikes for some model/kernel combos (not all). Customer reports and internal alerts suggest regression is most visible on mixed-shot chat workloads with many short prompts interleaved with a few long contexts. Need a reproducible method to surface kernel heuristics misfires and cache-eviction interactions.

What we mean by "serpentine effect"
-----------------------------------
- When the input stream order is monotonic (all short then all long) the runtime's heuristic caches and batching behave as expected.
- When order alternates short/long/short/long, we observed throughput jitter and increased kernel selection oscillation (scheduler swaps kernels mid-run).
- "Serpentine sweep" = purposely randomizing input lengths and ordering permutations to stress cache packing, KV reuse, and kernel decision boundaries.

Workloads tested
----------------
- Chat-mix-small: N=2000, 80% short (<=64 tokens), 20% short-with-history (<=128 tokens)
- Chat-mix-longburst: N=1200, 60% short, 30% long (512–1024 tokens), 10% very long (>=1500 tokens)
- LLM-bench-multi: collection of 8 models (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-small, Falcon-7B, internal-compat-13B, 2 research open models) using deterministic prompts (50 per model)
- Eval set for quality: 200 multi-choice and 100 code completions (for SNR of model degradation)

Kernels & Quant configs
----------------------
- Baseline: fp32 (reference) + our standard kernel schedule (v12)
- INT8: static per-layer quant + kernel set K-int8-v3 (vector-lane packing enabled)
- FP8: e4m3 path (cuda_cast path) + kernel set K-fp8-v2 (packed-GEMM)
- GPTQ: 4-bit GPTQ skeleton using K-gptq-v1 kernel (fallbacks to int8 for some ops)
- AWQ: AWQ-optimized kernels (K-awq-v1) with per-tensor scale caching enabled

Benchmarking approach (serpentine sweep)
--------------------------------------
1) Generate 10 permutations of each workload where prompt length ordering is a different seeded shuffle (preserve the per-workload length distribution).
2) Run each permutation 5 times (fresh process each time) to capture cold-start variability.
3) Capture: tokens/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory high-water, kernel-switch-count, KV-cache-hit-rate, and a simple quality delta (multi-choice accuracy drop relative to fp32).
4) Run on two instance types: A100 80GB (CUDA 12) and H100-PCIe (CUDA 12.1) to detect arch-specific kernel heuristics.

Representative command (internal runner)
---------------------------------------
python bench_runner.py --workload chat-mix-longburst --perm-seed 17 --retries 1 --model llama-2-13b --kernels int8,fp8,gptq,awq,fp32 --capture metrics.json

Key observations (summary)
------------------------
- INT8 (K-int8-v3) generally improves average tokens/s by 18–32% vs fp32, but p95 tails increased by 6–12% on mixed-length serpentine permutations. Kernel-switch-count correlated with p95 spikes.
- FP8 (K-fp8-v2) delivered the best avg throughput on H100 (30–40% improvement) and more stable tails than INT8 on A100, likely due to the GPU's fp8 math throughput.
- AWQ had the smallest average quality delta (multi-choice accuracy drop ~0.6% vs fp32) but showed two failure modes: (a) occasional kernel fallback thrashing when encountering rare op patterns (softmax variants), and (b) KV-cache eviction penalties when long sequences cause block remapping.
- GPTQ delivered the lowest memory footprint and competitive throughput for long-context batches, but quality delta was higher on code tasks (~2.9% dropout) unless per-layer re-scaling was used.
- The worst p95 regressions correlate with: (1) kernel-switch-count > 5 per second, and (2) KV-cache-hit-rate dipping below 70%.

Small reproducible case (short/long alternation)
------------------------------------------------
- Setup: llama-2-13b, sequence order alternation short(32)/long(1024) repeated 100 times.
- Result: INT8 run saw kernel-switch bursts after ~20 iterations; tokens/s dropped by ~22% for 10 seconds then recovered. Captured stack traces show scheduling pre-emption in CUDA streams when packed-GEMM tried to reallocate temp buffers.

Hypotheses
----------
1) The kernel selection heuristic is too sensitive to instantaneous sequence-length distribution and lacks hysteresis -> causes oscillation under serpentine inputs.
2) Some kernels (especially vector-packed INT8) have a heavier temporary allocation pattern that, when combined with irregular batch shapes, triggers CUDA driver-level serialization which shows as p95 spikes.
3) KV cache eviction/repacking for long contexts is not accounted for in the kernel cost model, so the router picks higher-throughput-but-higher-eviction kernels.

Proposed mitigations (short term)
--------------------------------
- Add a 1s hysteresis window into kernel selection: prefer previous kernel for small windows unless throughput regressions are sustained.
- Limit per-request kernel-switches to at most 1 per request; treat switches as an expensive op (penalize in scheduler cost).
- Instrument temporary allocation counts and sizes in the runtime to expose which kernels allocate scratch buffers frequently.
- In batch builder, prefer packing inputs by length-clusters with a serpentine-aware sampler: if frequent alternation detected, bias to mini-batches that group small lengths together for a short window.

Longer-term work
----------------
- Re-train kernel cost model to include KV-cache impact estimate (eviction penalties) and temporary allocation overhead.
- Kernel authors: examine INT8 packing path for reusable workspace pattern to avoid repeated cudaMalloc / free on common batch-size transitions.
- Add a fuzzing suite that runs serpentine permutations against new kernel commits as part of CI (fail on >5% p95 regression vs baseline).

Concrete next steps / action items (owners)
------------------------------------------
- Marco: add kernel-switch counter metric to exporter + tag per-request (ETA 1 week).
- Ellen: prototype 1s hysteresis and evaluate stable 10k-run on A100 (ETA 2 weeks).
- Ravi: instrument temporary allocation sizes in the runtime and run targeted microbench for packed-GEMM (ETA 1 week).
- Aisha (me): consolidate serpentine runner into bench_runner and add serpentine-permutation fixture; create CI job draft (ETA 2 weeks).

Open questions / unknowns
------------------------
- Are there other drivers (CUDA or driver-level) causing occasional stream serialization not visible in our traces? Need to capture nvprof traces on a failing run.
- How do different memory allocators (jemalloc vs cudaMalloc) interact with packed kernels on H100? Worth trying tlmalloc variants.

Appendix: raw sample numbers (chat-mix-longburst, A100)
-----------------------------------------------------
- fp32 baseline: tokens/s 62.3, p95 latency 210ms, mem HW 44GB, quality delta 0.0%
- INT8 (K-int8-v3): tokens/s 78.5 (+26%), p95 236ms (+12%), mem HW 28GB, quality delta +1.7%
- FP8 (K-fp8-v2): tokens/s 81.3 (+30%), p95 219ms (+4%), mem HW 30GB, quality delta +0.9%
- AWQ (K-awq-v1): tokens/s 75.6 (+21%), p95 248ms (+18% but intermittent), mem HW 26GB, quality delta +0.6%
- GPTQ (K-gptq-v1): tokens/s 70.1 (+12.5%), p95 225ms (+7%), mem HW 22GB, quality delta +2.9% (code tasks)

Notes on reproducibility
-----------------------
- All runs used the same docker image: redwood/serving-runtime:nightly-202503. CUDA and driver versions are documented in linked confluence page.
- Seeds and permutation lists saved under mnt/bench-artifacts/serpentine/2025-03-12/*

End-of-doc quick checklist
-------------------------
- [ ] Add nvprof trace capture to failing permutations.
- [ ] Add CI serpentine smoke job.
- [ ] Review INT8 packing workspace allocations with kernel authors.
- [ ] Re-run the longburst tests on H100 with FP8 baseline and compare.

If you reproduce, paste the runner log into the Confluence page linked above and tag the ticket CON-1423.
